status.label: Reproducible symptom; diagnostics needed
status.detail: Alt-based Keyboard Manager remaps miss the first chord after Alt is released, while Ctrl and Shift mappings work. The report lacks the exact Windows build and a bug-report archive needed to distinguish an OS input change from PowerToys state handling.

next_action.label: Collect input-state diagnostics
next_action.reason: The symptom is specific, but implementation design would be speculative without exact OS and remap configuration evidence.

actions.label: Ask for Keyboard Manager diagnostics

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed Alt-key reproduction. Could you attach a PowerToys bug-report ZIP and confirm your exact Windows build (`winver`), whether the problem affects Left Alt, Right Alt, or both, and whether it reproduces in Notepad? Please also include a screenshot of one affected remap and say whether PowerToys or the target app is running elevated. If practical, confirm whether uninstalling the suspected Windows update changes the behavior.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

judgment.rationale: The first-chord-only failure after releasing Alt is a strong, testable symptom, but the current evidence does not identify whether it is limited to one Alt key, an elevation boundary, a target application, or a specific Windows input-stack update.
evidence: Alt+H/J/K/L remaps reportedly worked before a recent Windows update.
The first Alt chord passes through unchanged; subsequent chords work until Alt is released.
Equivalent Ctrl or Shift mappings reportedly work.
No bug-report ZIP, exact Windows build, remap screenshot, elevation state, or neutral-app reproduction is attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Collect the exact Windows build, affected Alt side, neutral-app and elevation results, remap configuration, and PowerToys diagnostics before investigating Keyboard Manager input-state code.
